If this cluster is lost, nobody can decrypt its backups until the recovery kit of the active key is downloaded and confirmed (or the key is escrowed in a KMS). Download every share, give each to a different person, then confirm the kit by pasting enough shares back.

The fleet registers these keys in its clusters by itself (also a new key before you activate it). Where its credential may not, use Establish trust on the cluster.
The cluster master key isn't set up yet: no control-plane member can hold a share of it. Join a node, or turn on the built-in control-plane member (LOADWEAVER_BUILTIN_MEMBER).
Only one key holder: the built-in control-plane member holds the master key alone. Add a node or a KMS, and back up the recovery kit and the control-plane state volume.

The built-in control-plane member keeps a standby copy of the master key, so it can take over when no node is left. A database dump together with the control-plane state volume can rebuild the key: protect both.
The built-in control-plane member's seal key doesn't match the registered one, so it can't open the master key. Mount the original control-plane state volume.
The built-in control-plane member can't read its seal key. Check the control-plane state volume or LOADWEAVER_BUILTIN_SEAL_KEY_FILE.
